$schema_note: MMBT benchmark-bundle manifest. Read this BEFORE drawing conclusions from any data in this directory. Status vocabulary: appendix = vendor-stack comparison, NOT part of the canonical cross-host ranking; preliminary = data present but grid not yet fully complete.
claim_scope: Vendor productized inference stack (Apple MLX, AMD dream-server bundled custom llama.cpp + ROCm 7) vs vanilla llama.cpp at b9151 on the SAME hardware that the canonical study measured. Single-user (conc=1) only. Multi-user, cross-host ranking, and cross-engine quality are out of scope.
relates_to: hardware-tests/qwen3.6-q8-fleet-2026-05-17 — this bundle answers the auditor's 'best-stack matrix' ask for Apple and AMD only. NVIDIA productized stack (vLLM/TensorRT-LLM) is covered by the canonical study's Tower2 vLLM appendix and is not re-covered here.

engines.name: Apple MLX (mlx-lm Python API)
engines.note: Driven via mlx_lm.stream_generate. Each cell's cell.json.engine_version records the installed version.

engines.name: dream-server bundled custom llama.cpp build
engines.fronted_by: Lemonade Server OpenAI-compatible API on port 11434, started with --llamacpp rocm flag
engines.note: NOT to be conflated with vanilla Lemonade SDK's bundled Vulkan binary at /opt/lemonade/llama/vulkan/; those directories exist but are empty in this container. The --llamacpp rocm flag routes Lemonade to /opt/llama-custom/, which is dream-server's downstream patch set.

prompt_corpus.note: Same SHA-pinned natural-English prompt corpus the canonical study used. Used here in both MLX and dream-server-rocm7 grids for direct comparability with canonical cells.

grid.scope_note: conc=1 only on purpose — buyer-relevant single-user claim. Multi-user (conc>=4) is out of scope here as in canonical.

datasets.load_bearing_for: Apple-MLX-vs-canonical-Metal lift claim for the 27B dense model.
Apple-MLX-vs-canonical-Metal lift claim for the 35B-A3B MoE model. The MLX lift is larger here than on the dense 27B, which is the more interesting half of the finding.

Demonstrates that ROCm 7 (dream-server's bundled build) loads and serves Qwen3.6-27B-Q8 on Strix Halo where the canonical study's pinned llama.cpp b9151 + ROCm 6.4.4 segfaulted. Also shows that this path's decode matches vanilla Vulkan within noise while prefill is significantly slower because the bundled engine is at an older upstream commit than b9151. The ctx=16K cell adds a long-context data point: TTFT = 185.6 s (vs canonical Vulkan ttft ~30 s at the same cell) — the older-engine prefill cost shows up most dramatically at long context.
